findings.description: Removing the `hasattr` fallback breaks uploads of file-like proxies that expose `read` through `__getattr__` on Python 3.12+. These objects support reading but fail the runtime protocol check.
findings.rationale: Pass a proxy wrapping `io.BytesIO` whose `__getattr__` delegates to the wrapped stream as a multipart file. On Python 3.12+, runtime protocol checks use static attribute lookup, so `isinstance(fp, _SupportsRead)` returns false although `fp.read()` works. The proxy is consequently passed as multipart data instead of being read, causing upload preparation to fail with a TypeError.

item.command: /bin/zsh -lc 'python -c $'"'from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable\\nfrom io import BytesIO\\n@runtime_checkable\\nclass SupportsRead(Protocol):\\n    def read(self, length: int = ..., /) -> bytes: ...\\nclass FileProxy:\\n    def __init__(self):\\n        self.file = BytesIO(b\"upload contents\")\\n    def __getattr__(self, name):\\n        return getattr(self.file, name)\\nf = FileProxy()\\nprint(\"hasattr:\", hasattr(f, \"read\"))\\nprint(\"protocol:\", isinstance(f, SupportsRead))\\nprint(\"read:\", f.read())'"

/bin/zsh -lc 'python -c $'"'from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable\\nfrom io import BytesIO\\n@runtime_checkable\\nclass SupportsRead(Protocol):\\n    def read(self, length: int = ..., /) -> bytes: ...\\nclass FileProxy:\\n    def __init__(self):\\n        self.file = BytesIO(b\"upload contents\")\\n    def __getattr__(self, name):\\n        return getattr(self.file, name)\\nf = FileProxy()\\nprint(\"hasattr:\", hasattr(f, \"read\"))\\nprint(\"protocol:\", isinstance(f, SupportsRead))\\nprint(\"read:\", f.read())'"

hasattr: True
protocol: False
